plan: My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $25, which maximizes my potential profit. If I win, I'll pay less than my bid (the third-highest bid), and if I win, I'll gain the difference between my value and the payment. Bidding above my true value risks losing money, while bidding below risks not winning when I could have profitably acquired the item.

My private value is $18. My goal is to maximize profit by winning only if the price is below my value. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders might have values higher or lower than mine. I'll bid strategically near my value - not exactly at $18, but slightly below to create a buffer. A bid around $16-$17 gives me a chance to win while protecting potential profit margin.

My private value is $31. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $31 ensures I only win if the item is truly worth more to me than others. If I win, I'll pay less than my bid. If I overbid, I risk paying more than the item's worth to me. With no prior round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid seems most rational.
